oncall-bot: INCIDENT ▸ SLO burn-rate alert triggered for service=runtime /route=/api/generate — burn=4.2x over 10m, 1.8x over 1h. Paging policy matched: page oncall. incident_id=INC-20251201-37
oncall-bot: auto-escalation timer started (10m)
Maya: taking pager — oncall to triage. ETA 5m to initial triage.
Maya: quick check — dashboards show 500ms p50 unchanged, but p99 spiked from 800ms->2.5s. Errors at 5xx increased by ~6%.
Ashwin: stack traces show KV cache misses spiking concurrently; looks like batching backlog + a small ML worker OOM earlier.
Zara: customer impact: a few support tickets reporting timeouts on heavy prompt workloads, not widespread yet.
Maya: mitigation attempt 1 — reduce batch max_tokens from 2048->1024 to lower tail latency. Pushing config to staging then prod.
Maya: logs: ``deploy-bot: config patch applied to pool-2: batching.max_tokens=1024``
Leo: running quick canary, watching p99 and queue depth.
Maya: canary looks better. Applying to remaining capacity.
SRE Lead: good — note: this is triggering the 10m burn rule which pages. We should consider multi-window adjustments; today the 10m window is too sensitive for known bursty RLHF workloads.
Ashwin: Agreed. Proposing change: keep page on 10m if burn>6x OR 10m burn AND sustained 1h burn>2x. That avoids paging on short noisy spikes.
Zara: +1 — but keep an alert for ops scoreboard so we still get visibility (no page). Add a non-pager incident channel.
Maya: draft of modified rule (pseudo):
```
alert: SLO_burn_multiwindow
expr: burn_rate_10m > 6 OR (burn_rate_10m > 4 AND burn_rate_1h > 2)
labels: severity:critical (only when 1h>2), severity:warning (when 10m>4 && 1h<=2)
pager: critical -> page oncall, warning -> slack #sre-observability
```
Ashwin: small nit: we already have policies about budget enforcement that say when 1h burn>2 we should also trigger leadership notify. Add label `notify:leadership` on that branch.
Maya: ack. Will open a follow-up PR to alerting rules.
ops-bot: NOTE: created ticket OPS-5923 "Adjust SLO burn paging rules for short bursts" assigned to Maya. Link: https://tracker.internal/OPS-5923
SRE Lead: also request new dashboard: multi-window burn chart (1m/5m/10m/1h) + queue depth + kv-cache-miss-rate. Put on the incident runbook as postmortem checklist.
Leo: I'll spin up the dashboard and add to observability library. ETA 4h.
Zara: Product note — need to measure customer-facing error rate separately (5xx vs timeout) to attribute SLA impact.
Maya: mitigation summary: applied batching reduction and rolled back one worker with repeated OOM. Tail latency and errors are trending down. Marking incident as mitigated for now.
oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE ▸ status=mitigated incident_id=INC-20251201-37
Maya: postmortem tasks: 1) update paging rule (PR) 2) create multi-window burn dashboard (Leo) 3) add KB entry on batching profiles and when to adjust 4) run a load test to validate new thresholds against bursty RLHF workloads.
Ashwin: sample alert rule snippet for PR:```
- alert: SLOBurnPager
  expr: (burn_10m > 6) or ((burn_10m > 4) and (burn_1h > 2))
  for: 2m
  annotations:
    runbook: https://runbooks/internal/slo-burn
  labels:
    team: runtime
    pager: "oncall"
```
Zara: I'll own the KB on customer impact classification.
Maya: leaving a follow-up in #postmortems with incident timeline. tagging @SRE Lead for review of paging policy changes.
SRE Lead: thanks all. Quick decision: make change behind a feature flag for 72h to monitor false negatives, then roll fully if stable.
Maya: noted. closing this thread, will update OPS-5923 with PR and dashboard links. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: Ticket OPS-5923 updated with comment: "PR #428 opened by Maya -> alerting rule + feature flag. Leo created dashboard draft."
